claim: A connectome model built from fMRI during a divergent thinking task predicted creative ability in held-out people; the predictive edges had hubs in default, salience and executive networks.
quote: frontal and parietal regions within default, salience, and executive brain systems
authors: Beaty, Kenett, Christensen, Rosenberg, Benedek, Chen, Fink, Qiu, Kwapil, Kane, Silvia
title: Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity
transfer: Descriptive. Suggests an agent needs both a free-association generator and a control/selection stage working together, but gives no step by itself.

claim: The high-creativity network had 224 positive edges with hubs in left posterior cingulate (default), left anterior insula (salience) and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (executive); the low-creativity network (603 edges) did not generalize reliably.
title: Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity
transfer: Descriptive. Salience as a switch suggests a router step that decides when to generate versus evaluate.

claim: During idea generation, default and salience regions were coupled early, and default-executive coupling rose at later stages, read as cooperation of spontaneous thought and cognitive control.
title: Default and Executive Network Coupling Supports Creative Idea Production
transfer: Concrete order: free generation first, then control-guided refinement of the same ideas. Matches a diverge-then-evaluate pipeline. Pre-2018 but the anchor for the field.

claim: Associative thinking is central to creativity; the review separates free from goal-directed association and links both to semantic and episodic memory systems, and says computational models of memory now let researchers study search strategies.
title: Associative thinking at the core of creativity
transfer: Two retrieval modes as two prompts: a free-association pass (loose, no goal) and a goal-directed pass (constrained to the task). Run both and compare.

claim: Semantic richness affects quantity and quality of ideas differently, and cognitive control helps idea production when conceptual knowledge is limited.
title: Costs and benefits of semantic memory structure for generating original ideas (title as reported by search result, Thinking & Reasoning; not verified)
transfer: Rich context may give more ideas but less original ones. Suggests testing a trimmed context for the generator on open tasks. Unconfirmed.

claim: Brain activity in a preparation interval before a problem predicts whether it will later be solved with insight or with analysis; EEG showed medial frontal (control) and temporal (semantic) differences.
title: The Prepared Mind
transfer: Only a state, not a step. Agent analogue: choose mode (broad vs analytic) before reading the problem details. Pre-2018.

claim: Insight solutions were preceded by a right parieto-occipital alpha increase and then a gamma burst about 300 ms before the solution; read as brief shutting out of input before a new association surfaces.
title: Aha: The cognitive neuroscience of insight (title as listed in search)
transfer: Descriptive. Hint: a pass with distractors removed (reduced input) before re-attempting. Weak transfer.

claim: In trials solved with insight, an alpha-dominant brain state was visited and kept more during preparation and solving than in analytic trials.
title: Dynamics of hidden brain states when people solve verbal puzzles
transfer: Descriptive. Supports two solving modes (insight vs analytic) that differ before the problem is seen.

claim: 40 Hz tACS over right temporal lobe raised accuracy on a verbal insight task (Compound Remote Associates) by about 19-20% vs sham; 10 Hz parietal tACS and the visuospatial Rebus task showed no significant effect.
quote: During γ-tACS over the right temporal lobe, we observed an increase in accuracy on a verbal insight task.
authors: Santarnecchi, Sprugnoli, Bricolo, Costantini, Liew, Musaeus, Salvi, Pascual-Leone, Rossi, Rossi
title: Gamma tACS over the temporal lobe increases the occurrence of Eureka! moments
transfer: None for software. Causal evidence that remote-association retrieval is a distinct process; small sample, authors note it may be general problem solving.

claim: A meta-analysis of 117 incubation studies found a small positive effect (d about 0.29); divergent tasks gained more than insight tasks, and an undemanding filler task beat both a demanding task and no break.
title: Does incubation enhance problem solving? A meta-analytic review
transfer: Concrete: a break step on open tasks, filled with a low-demand unrelated task, then return. For an LLM this means a fresh-context re-sample. Pre-2018 but the core effect-size source.

claim: A finding that undemanding tasks raise mind wandering and creative gains did not replicate, and later studies found no link between incubation mind wandering and creative improvement; the mechanism remains unclear.
authors: as summarized in a search result for an open-access paper (exact paper not opened)
title: Incubation and mind wandering paper (PMC9053813 or PMC4956660; exact title not verified)
transfer: Warning: do not build an agent step on 'mind wandering causes insight'. Test any incubation step empirically. Source identity unverified.

claim: Aha experiences raise belief in unrelated statements shown right after a solved anagram, even false ones (d = .629 in the strongest case), so the feeling of insight is a heuristic that can mislead.
title: The dark side of Eureka: Artificially induced Aha moments make facts feel true
transfer: Concrete guard: a sudden confident insight is not evidence. Require an external check before accepting a breakthrough answer. Fits our ARC result of being fooled by programs that fit every example.

claim: A preregistered study found a positive link between Aha strength and accuracy on problems that need implicit processing, using a continuous real-time insight measure.
title: Getting a grip on insight: real-time and embodied Aha experiences predict correct solutions
transfer: Insight confidence carries some signal on hard puzzles. Combine with item 12: a weak prior, never a stopper.

claim: Insight may be used as a fast heuristic for judging ideas, creating an insight fallacy where an idea is taken as true because it felt like an insight; critics say the insight-accuracy link may not be causal.
authors: Laukkonen, Schooler, Tangen; Webb, Laukkonen, Cropper, Little
title: The Eureka Heuristic (preprint); commentary on Danek and Salvi 2018
transfer: Same as item 12: separate felt confidence from verification.

claim: Semantic distance from five semantic models, combined into one factor, predicts human creativity ratings across tasks and reproduces the serial order effect (later responses more original).
title: Automating creativity assessment with SemDis
transfer: Concrete and cheap: score each candidate by embedding distance from the obvious answers; keep generating past the first few ideas because originality rises with order.

claim: fMRI of 170 people on the Alternate Uses Task compared with LLMs of 270M to 72B parameters: alignment with the default mode network rises with model size, and alignment with default and frontoparietal networks rises with idea originality, strongest early in the creative process.
quote: Brain-LLM alignment increases with model size, but only in the default mode network.
authors: Ismayilzada, Luchini, Gokce, AlKhamissi, Bosselut, Laverghetta, van der Plas, Beaty
title: Large Language Models Align with the Human Brain during Creative Thinking
transfer: Descriptive. Implication: early prompt-stage representations carry the creative signal, so diversity should be injected at the start, not by late editing.

claim: A reasoning-trained model variant showed the opposite alignment pattern to a creativity-tuned one, which the authors read as chain-of-thought training moving representations toward analytical processing and away from creative neural patterns.
quote: suggesting chain-of-thought training moves representations away from creative neural patterns and toward analytical processing
title: Large Language Models Align with the Human Brain during Creative Thinking
transfer: Matches our finding that reasoning scaffolds help puzzles and hurt open tasks. Route: use a non-reasoning, high-temperature path for diverge mode. Quote comes from a fetch-tool summary of the abstract, not raw page text.

claim: A two-phase prompt that separates free creative exploration from constraint satisfaction gave significantly higher diversity and novelty with high utility than baselines, and yielded more distinct outputs as samples grew.
quote: decoupling creative exploration from constraint satisfaction
title: Divergent-Convergent Thinking in Large Language Models for Creative Problem Generation (CreativeDC)
transfer: Direct recipe: phase 1 explore with no task constraints, phase 2 pick one and fit constraints. Mirrors the default-then-executive order. Fits our NoveltyBench gain.

claim: Advanced reasoning strategies such as MCTS and self-correction gave no significant improvement in LLM creativity on code generation, and the best model (GPT-4) still fell short of human creativity.
quote: observe no significant improvement in creativity
authors: Lu, Wang, Li, Jiang, Khudanpur, Jiang, Khashabi
title: Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation
transfer: Generic evaluate-and-revise does not create novelty. Their denial prompting (forbid earlier solutions, ask again) is a concrete forced-divergence step.

claim: Two preregistered experiments with 1,100 people found LLM help boosts creativity during assisted tasks but may hurt later unassisted creative performance.
quote: may inadvertently hinder independent creative performance when users work without assistance
title: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking
transfer: None for the single agent; relevant to the later multi-person design (people may lose independent ideas).

claim: A September 2026 preprint reports human-like serial order effects (later ideas more original) in Alternate Uses Task outputs of a range of LLMs; not peer reviewed and exploratory.
title: LLM serial order effects on the Alternate Uses Task (title not verified)
transfer: If true, asking for many ideas in one run and keeping the later ones is a cheap diverge step. Page returned 403; unverified.

claim: No study was found that tests incubation, mind wandering or an aha moment as a deliberate step in an LLM agent loop; TACIT (single author, cs.LG) maps model behavior to impasse and an aha point but its text could not be read.
title: TACIT: Transformation-Aware Capturing of Implicit Thought
transfer: Gap. An incubation step in our agent would be new and needs our own test. Search budget ran out before more LLM-side queries.
